content.title: About
content.content: Breadsticks are crunchy, hard sticks made from gluten‑free flour (rice, corn or buckwheat). They are suitable for people with celiac disease and those who prefer a firmer texture. The product contains no gluten but retains a traditional bread flavor thanks to fermented starters.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gluten‑free breadsticks are often used as a substitute for regular croutons in gluten‑free cooking.
Their firm texture makes them perfect for dipping into sauces, soups, and salads.
In some countries they are traditionally served alongside seafood dishes.
Manufacturers frequently add sunflower or pumpkin seeds to boost flavor and nutrition.
Gluten‑free versions appeared in the early 2000s in response to growing demand for gluten‑free foods.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Suitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity, eliminating the risk of intestinal inflammation.

items.title: Low sugar
items.content: Most varieties contain no added sugar, making them appropriate for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Gluten‑free flour provides a slow release of energy, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Added seeds and whole‑grain gluten‑free flour increase dietary fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: The crisp texture is achieved without excessive oil, keeping the product relatively low in calories.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some versions may contain nuts, seeds, or soy lecithin, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: To enhance flavor the product is often salted; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Hard texture
items.content: May pose a choking hazard for young children; break into small pieces before serving.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Certain manufacturers use preservatives and flavor enhancers; choose options with minimal ingredient lists.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Breadsticks can be enjoyed as a snack, served with soups, salads, dips, or used as a crunchy base for appetizers. They are easy to break into pieces and pair well with olive oil, hummus, guacamole, or cheese sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store breadsticks in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator to prevent moisture absorption and loss of crunch. Discard any sticks that become soft, moldy, or develop an off‑odor.
